title: Powerbuilding is an Abomination.
summary: NH argues powerbuilding fails at both strength and size. It centres on the arbitrary powerlifting big three, uses short-range strength technique and 1RM training, and treats isolation work as pump-chasing accessories. His fix is to drop the big-three focus and 1RM training and train every muscle seriously close to failure, which he says is simply classic bodybuilding.
claims: Powerbuilding pairs the big three, heavy and low-rep, with high-rep bodybuilding accessories; it sounds reasonable but usually delivers neither strength nor size
Powerbuilding trains one very specific kind of strength, 1RM on three lifts, so why powerlifting and not weightlifting or strongman as the strength half?
Even if the big three beat weightlifting lifts for size, they lose to bodybuilding lifts: dips and push-ups over bench, RDLs over deadlifts, hack squats over squats
Bodybuilding alternatives beat the big three on stimulus-to-fatigue, range of motion, tendon strain and CNS fatigue
Many bodybuilders report their chest or quads grew after dropping the bench or squat; the big three are overrated for hypertrophy
Not everyone is built for the squat, bench and deadlift, yet powerbuilding forces them on everyone
Most powerbuilders never compete, so they have no reason to stick to the big three
Powerlifting technique minimises range of motion and maximises explosiveness (arched bench, low-bar, sumo), the opposite of what builds muscle
You would grow more from Romanian deadlifts than from sumo deadlifts
1RM strength is a specific skill that must dominate your program, so it takes energy away from everything else
Most powerbuilders end up as unstructured 'max-out bros' with no peaking or deloads, or as 'powerlifters who do curls'
'Chasing the pump' devalues isolation work; random light curls for 15 reps far from failure won't build anything
If you treat arms, core, rear delts and lats as accessories, they will look like accessories; treat curls like a main lift
If you call yourself a powerbuilder you have no excuse to skip any muscle; skipping muscles with no carryover is powerlifting
The idea that compounds are low-rep strength work and isolations are high-rep hypertrophy work is false and harms naturals
The hypertrophy rep range is 3-15 reps; low-rep sets of 3-5 or 5-8 work for size too
The only real differences between rep ranges are training intensity and volume accumulation; a separate 'hypertrophy rep range' doesn't exist
The only difference between training for strength and for size is focus: strength is either the end or the means
A bodybuilder tracks loads exactly and adds weight or reps every session, using strength as a means to keep challenging the muscle
Fix 1: don't focus on the big three; bench is just a horizontal press chosen because it is easier to judge than dips
Fix 2: don't train for 1RM strength; every max-out costs you muscle-building capacity, though low reps are still fine
Fix 3: train every muscle seriously, take everything to or close to failure, and progressively overload
Apply those fixes and you are just bodybuilding, as the silver and bronze era bodybuilders trained: strong, varied rep ranges, every muscle
Lifters should stop calling themselves powerbuilders out of shame and reclaim the word bodybuilding
exercises: suboptimal for hypertrophy vs dips or push-ups
better than conventional or sumo deadlift for growth
better hypertrophy profile than back squat
